claim_text: Two kiwis before bed may support sleep quality.
approved_wording: Eating two kiwifruit about one hour before bed may support sleep quality for some people as part of a bedtime routine, but evidence is limited.
allowed_context: Video scripts about kiwi as a bedtime-food routine.
required_caveats: Not a cure for insomnia; not senior-specific proof; ask clinician for chronic insomnia, sleep apnea symptoms, serious daytime sleepiness, or sleep medication concerns.
forbidden_wording: cures insomnia; proven for every senior; works overnight; replaces sleep medicine; guaranteed sleep

claim_text: Persistent insomnia needs medical care beyond food advice.
approved_wording: Persistent insomnia, loud snoring, breathing pauses, restless legs, or daytime sleepiness should be discussed with a clinician; food routines do not replace medical care.
allowed_context: Sleep-related videos with food, routine, supplement, or behavior advice.
required_caveats: Include when video mentions insomnia, serious sleep symptoms, sleep medication, or older adults with persistent sleep problems.
forbidden_wording: ignore sleep apnea; stop sleep medicine; food fixes chronic insomnia

approved_wording: People with kiwi allergy or latex-fruit reactions should avoid kiwi unless cleared by a clinician.
allowed_context: Any kiwi food video or kiwi routine recommendation.
required_caveats: Mention mouth itching, swelling, throat symptoms, known allergy, or latex-fruit reactions when relevant.
forbidden_wording: kiwi is safe for everyone; allergy-proof; harmless fruit for all seniors

claim_text: Kiwi contains natural sugar and potassium.
approved_wording: Kiwifruit is a fruit with natural sugar, fiber, vitamin C, and potassium; people with diabetes, kidney disease, or potassium restrictions should follow their care plan or ask a clinician.
allowed_context: Kiwi nutrition descriptions and senior food routines.
required_caveats: Use diabetes carbohydrate caveat and kidney or potassium restriction caveat when recommending daily use.
forbidden_wording: free food for diabetes; unlimited kiwi; safe for all kidney patients

claim_text: DASH-style eating supports blood pressure control.
approved_wording: A low-sodium DASH-style eating pattern can support blood pressure control; it should not be framed as a cure or medication replacement.
allowed_context: Blood-pressure videos, breakfast pattern videos, low-sodium diet guidance.
required_caveats: Medication users, kidney disease, potassium restriction, diabetes, and individualized sodium needs require clinician guidance.
forbidden_wording: cures hypertension; replace blood-pressure medicine; instantly lowers blood pressure; guaranteed normal blood pressure

claim_text: Lower sodium plus DASH can improve blood-pressure results.
approved_wording: The strongest results came when DASH-style eating was paired with lower sodium, but this is still dietary support, not medication replacement.
allowed_context: Blood-pressure nutrition scripts and food pattern comparisons.
required_caveats: Do not advise medication changes; caution for individualized sodium needs and clinical conditions.
forbidden_wording: salt trick cures blood pressure; stop medicine if you eat low sodium; guaranteed drop

claim_text: Oats provide soluble fiber that supports cardiovascular risk factors.
approved_wording: Oats bring soluble fiber that supports cardiovascular risk factors, especially cholesterol-related markers; do not present oats as a direct blood-pressure cure.
allowed_context: Heart-health breakfast scripts and DASH-style meal examples.
required_caveats: Diabetes portions and swallowing or dental limitations when relevant.
forbidden_wording: oats cure blood pressure; oats replace statins; overnight artery cleanse
